ifu.device_name: System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual
intended_use: The Ion System Cart (referred to as the System Cart) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract.
The Ion Controller (referred to as the Controller) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract.

The Ion Fully Articulating Catheter (referred to as the Catheter) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system for navigating to the target region in the airways. It is intended to also provide a conduit for the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe, Flexision Biopsy Needles and delivering compatible off-the-shelf tools.
The Flexision Biopsy Needle is intended to retrieve tissue from a target structure.
The Ion Peripheral Vision Probe (referred to as the Vision Probe) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system to provide live airway view for catheter navigation.
The Vision Probe Adapter is intended to be used to connect the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter.
The Vision Probe Bag is used for temporary storage of the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe during a procedure.
The Catheter Guide is intended to be used with the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to provide support.
The Sensor Connection Cleaner is used for cleaning the sensor connections on the carriage of the Ion System Cart and the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter.
The Swivel Connector is intended to be used to connect the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to an endotracheal tube.
The Suction Adapter is intended to allow modulation of suction when suction tubing is connected to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter.
Only physicians with adequate training and experience in bronchoscopic techniques and adequate healthcare facilities should perform procedures with the Ion endoluminal system.

Training provided by Intuitive is limited to the use of the Ion endoluminal system and does not replace the necessary medical training and experience required to perform diagnostic and therapeutic bronchoscopy procedures.
indications_for_use: The Ion endoluminal system (Model IF1000), referred to in this manual as "the system," assists the user in navigating a catheter and endoscopic tools in the pulmonary tract using endoscopic visualization of the tracheobronchial tree for diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. The Ion endoluminal system enables fiducial marker placement. It does not make a diagnosis and is not for pediatric use.
The PlanPoint Software uses patient CT scans to create a 3D plan of the lung and navigation pathways for use with the Ion endoluminal system.
The Flexision Biopsy Needle is used with the Ion endoluminal system to biopsy tissue from a target area in the lung.

warnings.section: Guidelines to Position the System Cart in the Procedure Room
warnings.text: To avoid patient injury, always lock the wheels of the System Cart before docking to the patient.

Do not use damaged or broken instruments or accessories. Inspect instruments and accessories for any defects such as unintended rough surfaces, sharp edges, or protrusions (for example, broken, cracked, chipped, or worn parts) prior to use. Failure to do so may result in patient harm.
To avoid patient injury, always lock the wheels of the System Cart before docking to the patient.
Perform system tests to ensure normal system operation and prevent patient injury such as pneumothorax.
Failure to properly install the Catheter and accessories may result in patient injury.
Do not contaminate instruments or accessories before or during use, as contamination may result in patient infection.
When docking to patient, always stabilize the endotracheal tube (ET tube). While docked, always release tension before adjusting ET tube as this may result in loss of ventilation.
Do not move patient bed after docking the system to the patient. Moving the patient bed may result in loss of ventilation pathway.

To prevent impaired ventilation and patient injury, the procedure should be performed under general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation, Electrocardiography (ECG) monitoring, and ventilator alarms.
Advance the Catheter only under live visualization from the Vision Probe (Live View) to prevent procedural delay or patient injury.
Do not activate the scroll wheel while interacting with the Controller touchscreen, as this may result in pneumothorax.
To prevent patient injury, do not use excessive force during the insertion or extraction of the Vision Probe, biopsy needle, or bronchoscopic tools through the Catheter tool channel.

When a system fault occurs, retract the tool inside the protective sheath immediately to minimize interaction with tissue and prevent patient injury as the Catheter slowly releaxes in response to the fault.
Insert the Vision Probe after biopsy to assess airways for trauma or bleeding to prevent delayed intervention in case of an emergency.
Always inspect the biopsy needle for damage before and during use. A damaged needle can contain loose fragments that may cause toxic reaction if left in the patient.
Use fluoroscopic visualization (fluoroscopy) when advancing tools past the tip of the Catheter. Failure to use fluoroscopy during biopsy may result in patient injury.

Always reset the needle stop (re-sheath the needle): before removing the biopsy needle from the Catheter tool channel, after preparing the sample, or before transferring the needle between staff. Failure to reset the needle stop during handling or hand-offs may result in infection or injury by needle stick.
If you notice damage to the inside of the Catheter during use, replace the Catheter. A damaged Catheter can contain loose fragments that may cause toxic reaction if left in the patient.
Failure to properly insert or remove forceps through the Catheter tool channel may damage the forceps, resulting in procedure delay or foreign body in the patient.
Clean and disinfect both the Controller and System Cart arm after each procedure to prevent cross-contamination that may result in infection.

When a system fault occurs, retract the tool inside the protective sheath immediately to minimize interaction with tissue and prevent patient injury as the Catheter slowly relaxes in response to the fault.

Use of this equipment adjacent to or stacked with other equipment should be avoided because it could result in improper operation. If such use is necessary, this equipment and the other equipment should be observed to verify that they are operating normally.

Before using the Ion endoluminal system (the system), review and understand the content in this manual and all accompanying manuals and supplements.
To prevent patient harm, use only instruments, accessories, and third-party products that are approved by Intuitive. Non-approved devices are not guaranteed to be compatible with the system.

Confirm that the sterile packaging for all singleuse devices is intact and sealed before use. Do not use contaminated singleuse devices or reuse singleuse devices, as this may result in patient infection or equipment damage.
To avoid risk of electric shock or equipment damage, do not step on, crush/ pinch, crimp, or otherwise stress cables and connectors.

Do not reuse or reprocess singleuse devices (such as the Swivel Connector and Vision Probe Adapter) after being removed from package, even if unused, as this may result in patient infection or device damage.
If the system, instruments and accessories, or any of their components cannot be manipulated in a precise and controlled manner, discontinue use and contact Intuitive to prevent patient harm.
In the event of a medical emergency, follow steps to obtain immediate access to the patient (emergency egress), to avoid delays in patient care.
Use caution during biopsy of targets within 5 mm of the visceral pleura or other critical structures. Biopsy near critical structures may result in patient injury.
Follow proper system and Controller cleaning procedures to prevent patient infection.
Properly disinfect the Controller to prevent infection.
Properly disinfect the arm to prevent infection.
